FLASHCARD SET · AGES 3–12 YEARS

Extra-curricular activity flashcards.

Forty-five clubs, forty-five first steps. Each card names one activity — chess, baking, pottery, robotics — and prints the two skills the club trains under its name, from Aim & Focus to Calm & Wellbeing. The fifteen youngest-friendly clubs are tagged Ages 3+; the rest are Ages 6+. Every club has a short page, a full lesson and a printable twin in the library — pick the club, learn the skill, and let the hobby grow.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    One club, one week

    Pick a single card — say, chess — and give it one honest week: learn one opening trick, play three games, teach someone the rules. A week of trying beats a month of deciding.

  2. 02

    Club fair night

    Deal five cards face down. Everyone draws one, names its two skills and pitches the club to the family in one minute — then vote on the one to try first.

  3. 03

    Skill scavenger hunt

    Read a card’s skill pill — Balance & Grace, Aim & Focus — and hunt for where the family already uses it: stairs, spoons, drawing straight lines. Every club trains something the house already does.

  4. 04

    Hobby diary

    After each club try-out, one journaling page: what we did, the best moment, keep or swap. Three honest entries later, the right club picks itself.

      Art Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 3+Make & build

      Art club is the maker’s hour: paint, paper, glue and whatever the imagination orders. The card prints the club’s two skills — Painting & Creativity — because art trains the hand and the idea at the same time. This card’s job: make the first painting feel easy, messy and worth framing.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Art club! Today we paint — any color, any idea. Painting & Creativity means there is no wrong picture. What will yours be?”

      Say it naturally, then wait. Whatever comes back — the word, the sound, a point, a giggle — is the right answer.

      Try this

      Tape three papers side by side and paint one thing across all three — a caterpillar, a rainbow, a long road. A painting that keeps going past the edge feels wonderfully rule-breaking.

      Quick parent note

      The word club comes from the old knot people tied — a clubby bunch, fastened together by the thing they love doing.

      Teach it, step by step

      This card belongs to a real class — open the Extra-Curricular Activities Flashcards (School Room) class on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Music Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 3+Perform & sing

      Music club is where the house finds its beat: pots, shakers, a keyboard, a lap that drumming works on. The card prints the club’s two skills — Rhythm & Sound — the pair every instrument, song and dance floor is built from. This card’s job: make the first five minutes of music feel like play, not practice.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Music club! Let’s find the beat — clap with me: one, two, one, two. Rhythm & Sound is the club’s secret pair. What sound can your hands make?”

      Try this

      Play echo claps: you clap a short pattern, the child claps it back, then swap. Two rounds in, let the child lead the pattern — leaders never want the game to end.

      Quick parent note

      Your heartbeat was the first rhythm you ever heard — four months before you were born, the drum was already playing.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Dance Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 3+Move & play

      Dance club is the room where feelings turn into steps: fast songs for zooming, slow songs for floating, no wrong moves on the floor. The card prints the club’s two skills — Movement & Expression — moving the body and telling the story inside it. This card’s job: get the first dance out before anyone feels shy.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Dance club! Put a song on and let your body listen. Movement & Expression — your arms can say happy, your knees can say silly. Show me!”

      Try this

      Freeze dance: dance while the song plays, freeze when it stops — and hold the freeze like a statue with a secret. Three songs later, everyone is warm and laughing.

      Quick parent note

      Dancers count music in eights — an eight-count — because most dance phrases are built in little eight-beat buildings.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Sports Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 3+Move & play

      Sports club is the team tryout for everything: ball games, running games, the games that need a buddy to be fun. The card prints the club’s two skills — Teamwork & Fitness — a strong body and the habit of playing WITH people. This card’s job: make moving together the favorite part of the week.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Sports club! Today we move as a team — roll the ball to me, I roll it back. Teamwork & Fitness: the ball travels, our legs travel, everybody wins.”

      Try this

      Set up a two-goal living-room soccer game with a soft ball and chair goals. Keep score out loud, shake hands after — the handshake is the real sport.

      Quick parent note

      The Olympic motto is three Latin words: faster, higher, stronger — together. The together was added in 2021.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Drama Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 3+Perform & sing

      Drama club is the pretend box, opened wide: characters, voices, a story that changes every time it is told. The card prints the club’s two skills — Stories & Confidence — inventing the tale and standing up to tell it. This card’s job: make speaking up feel like playing.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Drama club! Pick a character — a dragon, a dentist, a detective. Stories & Confidence means the story is yours. How does your character walk?”

      Try this

      Play story suitcase: grab three random objects and invent the story that connects them — the spoon, the shoe and the teddy bear were all on the same picnic.

      Quick parent note

      Actors say break a leg instead of good luck because theater people believe wishing luck out loud jinxes it.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Gardening Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 3+Cook, grow & help

      Gardening club is the slowest, most patient club in the school: a seed, a pot, water, and days of watching. The card prints the club’s two skills — Nature & Care — meeting the living world and taking care of it. This card’s job: plant the first pot and the first bit of patience together.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Gardening club! We plant the seed, we water it, and then we wait. Nature & Care — gardens teach waiting better than anyone. Where should our pot live?”

      Try this

      Plant a bean in a clear cup against the side so the root is visible. Water it, name it, and check it every morning — first sprouts arrive in about a week.

      Quick parent note

      A sunflower can grow taller than a grown-up in a single summer — faster than most children, which every gardener finds unfair.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Cooking Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 3+Cook, grow & help

      Cooking club is the kitchen, handed over: stirring, pouring, spreading, tasting — real food, made by small hands. The card prints the club’s two skills — Food & Independence — knowing what food is and being able to make some yourself. This card’s job: give the child one dish they can honestly say they cooked.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Cooking club! Today you are the chef — I am the helper. Food & Independence means you make the choices: stir, pour, taste. What do we cook first?”

      Try this

      Build-your-own faces: a rice cake, spread, and fruit pieces for eyes, noses and silly smiles. The chef assembles, the chef eats, the chef is extremely proud.

      Quick parent note

      Chefs taste as they cook — a bite, a thought, more salt — because a recipe is a plan, but the tongue is the boss.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Ballet Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 3+Move & play

      Ballet club is the quiet strength club: pointed toes, slow arms, a posture that looks like floating and feels like work. The card prints the club’s two skills — Balance & Grace — holding still and moving soft. This card’s job: make the very first positions feel like a costume the body wears.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Ballet club! Arms round like a bubble, heels together — first position. Balance & Grace: dancers are strong AND gentle. Can you stand like a dancer?”

      Try this

      Practice the tiptoe walk across the hallway — a plate of pretend hot soup balanced on one hand, slow steps, no spills. Ballet is secretly balance training in disguise.

      Quick parent note

      Ballet words are French because the rules of ballet were written down in France three hundred years ago — plié means bent.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Yoga Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 3+Move & play

      Yoga club is the slow-down club: stretches that become animals, breaths that count, a quiet the body makes on purpose. The card prints the club’s two skills — Calm & Wellbeing — a peaceful body and a peaceful mood, trained together. This card’s job: turn wiggly energy into tall tree pose and one long breath.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Yoga club! Feet down like roots, hands together up high — tree pose. Calm & Wellbeing: yoga is how bodies say ahh. How long can you hold it?”

      Try this

      Animal breaths: snake hiss (long and slow), lion roar (big exhale), bunny sniffs (three quick ones). Breathing becomes a game the body asks for at bedtime.

      Quick parent note

      Yoga poses were named after things their inventors watched — tree, cat, cow, mountain — a whole zoo and landscape hiding in one class.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Swimming Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 3+Move & play

      Swimming club is the water class: kicks, floats, blows bubbles and the slow brave work of letting go of the wall. The card prints the club’s two skills — Confidence & Safety — feeling strong in water and knowing its rules. This card’s job: make the pool a place the child walks toward, not away from.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Swimming club! Water has rules and we know them: never alone, always a grown-up watching. Confidence & Safety — brave AND careful. Ready to blow bubbles?”

      Try this

      Practice pool rules on dry land: walk by the pool (never run), enter feet first, and the grown-up-on-the-step game — swim TO someone, not AWAY from everyone.

      Quick parent note

      Swimming is the only sport that could save your life — which is why so many countries put it on the school timetable.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Reading Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 3+Read & write

      Reading club is the everywhere club: a couch, a bed, a bus seat — any book opens a branch. The card prints the club’s two skills — Imagine & Learn — pictures the mind makes and facts it collects, page after page. This card’s job: make ten minutes with a book the easiest appointment on the calendar.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Reading club! Pick the book, pick the spot — your lap is the library today. Imagine & Learn: books are movies for your brain. Which page should we stop on to guess?”

      Try this

      Read a page, then each person predicts what happens next — closest guess picks the next book. Prediction turns listening into a sport.

      Quick parent note

      The habit has a name people trust: bibliophiles love books so much the word literally means book-things — collectors of pages.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Crafts Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 3+Make & build

      Crafts club is the box of leftovers that builds anything: paper tubes, buttons, ribbon, a glue stick with plans. The card prints the club’s two skills — Make & Explore — turning materials into things and trying ideas without fear. This card’s job: prove that the recycling bin is a craft store in disguise.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Crafts club! Grab the box — tubes, paper, stickers, string. Make & Explore: we build the thing, then we build a better thing. What should today’s creature be?”

      Try this

      The tube zoo challenge: five cardboard tubes, five animals, one shelf for the grand opening. Every zookeeper names their animals — names are the finishing touch.

      Quick parent note

      The oldest known craft is bead jewelry — some shell beads are older than 100,000 years, made by hands that liked pretty things too.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Drawing Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 3+Make & build

      Drawing club is the looking club: a pencil, a page, and the habit of studying things until they can be drawn. The card prints the club’s two skills — See & Create — noticing the real and making the new. This card’s job: turn drawing from a talent people have into a practice people do.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Drawing club! First we look, then we draw — look at the apple: round, with a little stem. See & Create: artists copy the world and invent their own. What do we draw first?”

      Try this

      Blind-contour game: draw your own hand WITHOUT looking at the paper, eyes on your fingers the whole time. The result looks hilarious — and teaches more than any neat drawing.

      Quick parent note

      Leonardo da Vinci filled thousands of notebook pages with drawings — and drew his left-handed, in mirror writing, just to be extra.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Baking Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 3+Cook, grow & help

      Baking club is the careful kitchen: cups and spoons, flour clouds, and the magic oven that turns dough into something the whole house smells. The card prints the club’s two skills — Measure & Create — exact amounts and the joy they become. This card’s job: make the child the official measurer of the family kitchen.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Baking club! Baking is a recipe-follower’s game: one cup, two teaspoons, level it off. Measure & Create — careful measuring makes the magic. Ready to pour?”

      Try this

      Muffin math: let the child measure and pour every ingredient, counting each scoop out loud. Half the learning is in the measuring; the other half is warm from the oven.

      Quick parent note

      Baking is chemistry you can eat: heat makes the flour and eggs set into a completely new food, the same change that makes mud into pottery.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Singing Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 3+Perform & sing

      Singing club is the instrument everyone already owns: a voice, a song, and the bravery to let it out loud. The card prints the club’s two skills — Voice & Confidence — the sound and the courage behind it. This card’s job: make the first loud, happy note feel like the whole point.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Singing club! Everybody has a voice and yours is the only one like it. Voice & Confidence: big breath, big sound, no shy notes. What song lives in you today?”

      Try this

      Sing the echo game: you sing a line, the child echoes it, then swap — and let the child invent a line for YOU to echo. Silly words welcome; confidence doubles.

      Quick parent note

      Singing together makes hearts literally sync — choir members’ heartbeats slow down and line up with the song’s rhythm.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Archery Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Move & play

      Archery club is the steady-hands sport: a bow, a target, and the long quiet breath between drawing and releasing. The card prints the club’s two skills — Aim & Focus — picking the target and holding everything still until the moment is right. This card is a real-range club: kids try it where coaches and gear are waiting.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Archery club! This one is a with-a-coach sport: real bows live with trained grown-ups. Aim & Focus — archers breathe slow and aim steady. At home we practice the aim; the arrows wait for the range.”

      Try this

      Home aim training, no arrows: toss beanbags at a hoop, roll socks into a laundry-basket bullseye, hold a pose for five slow breaths before every throw. Focus first; bow later.

      Quick parent note

      Olympic archers aim with both eyes open and let go on the exhale — the same trick marksmen, surgeons and photographers all borrow.

      Staying safe

      Ask a grown-up and a trained coach — real bows and arrows need a proper range, safety gear and expert eyes before any arrow flies.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Astronomy Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Think & solve

      Astronomy club is the look-up club: stars, planets, the moon’s nightly shape shift and the questions that come with them. The card prints the club’s two skills — Wonder & Discovery — the big questions and the patient looking that answers them. This card’s job: make the night sky feel like a neighborhood.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Astronomy club! Tonight the ceiling is the sky — stars, the moon, a planet or two. Wonder & Discovery: astronomers ask big questions and look, look, look. Find the moon with me.”

      Try this

      Moon diary: draw the moon’s shape every night for two weeks in the same little notebook. Halfway through, the child predicts the next shape — and is usually right.

      Quick parent note

      Starlight is old news: the light from the brightest stars left years before it reached your eyes — some of it before your grandparents were born.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Bird Watching Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Think & solve

      Bird watching club is the quiet hunt: binoculars, a window, a park bench, and the patience to let birds forget you are there. The card prints the club’s two skills — Observe & Discover — watching closely and naming what appears. This card’s job: turn the daily birds outside into neighbors with names.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Bird watching club! Voices down, eyes up — what flew past? Observe & Discover: watchers look for color, size, song. Our first three birds get names in the notebook.”

      Try this

      Window tally: a paper by the window with three bird drawings. Every visit gets a tally mark. By Friday the family knows exactly who the regulars are.

      Quick parent note

      Crows can recognize individual human faces for years — the birds outside your window may already know exactly who you are.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Calligraphy Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Read & write

      Calligraphy club is the slow-writing art: a special pen, thick-and-thin strokes, and letters treated like small drawings. The card prints the club’s two skills — Letters & Patience — beautiful shapes and the calm they ask for. This card’s job: make the first swirly letter the proudest thing on the page.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Calligraphy club! Slow pens write the prettiest letters — downstrokes thick, upstrokes thin. Letters & Patience: we write ONE letter today and we write it ten times, beautifully.”

      Try this

      Fill one page with a single letter, huge, then tiny, then fancy — a whole family of A’s (or the child’s own initial). Sign the page like an artist signs a print.

      Quick parent note

      Before printing presses, every book was written by hand by scribes — a whole Bible could take one person years, one letter at a time.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Chess Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Think & solve

      Chess club is the board of six armies: pawns, knights, a king to protect and a plan to build. The card prints the club’s two skills — Focus & Strategy — thinking ahead and holding the whole board in your head. This card’s job: get the first game played and the first checkmate understood.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Chess club! Every piece has a job — the knight jumps, the rook runs straight, the king is precious. Focus & Strategy: good players think before they touch. What is your plan?”

      Try this

      Learn pawn chess first: pawns only, first to reach the far side wins. One game teaches how the littlest pieces do the biggest work.

      Quick parent note

      The number of possible chess games is bigger than the number of atoms in the observable universe — mathematicians checked.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Choir Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Perform & sing

      Choir club is singing with company: many voices, one song, parts that fit together like a puzzle. The card prints the club’s two skills — Voice & Harmony — your own sound and the magic of blending it. This card’s job: prove that a group of singers becomes one big instrument.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Choir club! Singing alone is a solo; singing together is a choir. Voice & Harmony: listen to your neighbor as much as yourself. Can we hold one long note — together?”

      Try this

      Round singing: one person starts a short song, a second starts the same song two lines later, and the two versions weave. Row Your Boat is the classic first round.

      Quick parent note

      Choirs sing in four classic parts — soprano, alto, tenor, bass — named centuries ago in Latin and Italian and still in use today.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Climbing Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Move & play

      Climbing club is the wall sport: holds, grips, a harness, and the slow brave choice of the next handhold. The card prints the club’s two skills — Courage & Movement — strong bodies and the nerve to move up. This card’s job: introduce the gym where ropes, helmets and trained belayers make climbing safe.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Climbing club! Walls are climbed with a plan — hand, hand, foot, foot. Courage & Movement: being brave does not mean rushing. At the gym, the rope team is trained; at home we train grips.”

      Try this

      Home grip and balance work: hang from a playground bar two seconds longer each day, walk a curb like a balance beam, plan three-point contact — always two hands and a foot or two feet and a hand.

      Quick parent note

      Rock climbers grade routes with numbers — and the world’s best climbers fall off the hardest ones dozens of times before they succeed.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Coding Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Make & build

      Coding club is the giving-instructions club: write steps clearly enough and the computer does exactly what you said — mistakes included, which is half the fun. The card prints the club’s two skills — Logic & Discovery — ordered thinking and the joy of finding what works. This card’s job: run the first program (no computer needed to start).

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Coding club! Computers follow instructions exactly — even the silly ones. Logic & Discovery: programmers write steps, test, fix, test again. Give ME the instructions: make a sandwich, step by step!”

      Try this

      Robot parent: the child writes or calls out exact steps, and you obey them literally — turn in circles when told circle, walk into the couch when the step was missing. Debugging begins at home.

      Quick parent note

      The first computer programmer was a mathematician named Ada Lovelace, who wrote an algorithm in the 1840s — before any computer existed to run it.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Cycling Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Move & play

      Cycling club is the two-wheel club: pedals, a helmet, and the specific pride of a vehicle you power yourself. The card prints the club’s two skills — Balance & Adventure — staying upright and going somewhere new. This card’s job: make the first wobbly meters feel like the freedom they are.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Cycling club! Helmet first, always. Balance & Adventure: eyes up, pedals round, and the bike rides under you. Where should our first ride go — the corner and back?”

      Try this

      Scoot-first learning: take the pedals off a small bike and let the child push with their feet, lifting both feet for glides. Balance arrives on its own; pedals reattach later like a promotion.

      Quick parent note

      The Tour de France covers more than three thousand kilometers — riders burn roughly six thousand calories a stage, breakfast twice and then some.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Debate Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Think & solve

      Debate club is the arguing-nicely club: pick a side, find your reasons, listen hard enough to answer kindly. The card prints the club’s two skills — Speak & Listen — clear talking and generous hearing. This card’s job: show that the best argument is the one that respects the other side.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Debate club! Today’s question: are dogs or cats the better pet? Speak & Listen — one voice at a time, everyone heard. Pick your side and give me your first reason.”

      Try this

      Family debate night with a silly question: summer or winter, pancakes or waffles. Two reasons each, then switch sides and argue the OTHER view — empathy with a timer.

      Quick parent note

      The word debate comes from Latin battuere, to fight — but good debaters fight with reasons, which is why the winners are often friends.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Fencing Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Move & play

      Fencing club is the sword sport with the strictest manners: salute first, mask on, then lightning feet. The card prints the club’s two skills — Agility & Focus — fast, light movement and total attention to one opponent. This card is a real-club sport: kids try it where masks, jackets and coaches are standard.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Fencing club! Fencers salute before every bout — respect first, sword second. Agility & Focus: quick feet, quiet mind. At home we practice footwork; the blades live at the club with the coach.”

      Try this

      Home footwork drills: the advance (step forward), the retreat (step back), the lunge (big step, front knee bent) — five of each, pillow on the head for posture. The coach supplies the sword.

      Quick parent note

      Fencing is one of only five sports in every modern Olympics since 1896 — and the masks were invented so fencers could argue less and duel more safely.

      Staying safe

      Ask a grown-up and a trained coach — blades, masks and jackets are fitted and checked by experts, and every bout happens under a coach’s eye.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Fashion Design Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Make & build

      Fashion design club is the wearable-ideas club: sketch a dress, choose the fabric, pin, cut, and — with a grown-up’s needle — make it real. The card prints the club’s two skills — Imagine & Create — designing in the head and building with the hands. This card’s job: make the first sketch feel like a real collection.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Fashion design club! Every outfit started as a drawing. Imagine & Create: designers sketch, choose fabric, and build. Design an outfit for rainy days — what should it do besides look great?”

      Try this

      Paper-doll runway: draw and cut three outfits for the same paper figure — rain, party, snow — then hold a runway show and explain each choice out loud.

      Quick parent note

      Fashion designers keep sketchbooks like detectives keep notebooks — a single flap or pocket in your jacket survived because somebody sketched it first.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Filmmaking Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Perform & sing

      Filmmaking club is the studio club: a story, a camera (any phone works), actors from the family, and a premiere on the couch. The card prints the club’s two skills — Imagine & Tell — inventing the scenes and getting them on screen. This card’s job: roll the very first take.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Filmmaking club! A film is a story with a camera — opening, middle, THE END. Imagine & Tell: directors plan the shots. Scene one: the dog walks in. Action!”

      Try this

      The one-minute documentary: film how a sandwich is really made, interview the chef, shoot the grand finale bite. Premiere after dinner, audience applauds, credits roll.

      Quick parent note

      A feature film is shot in thousands of tiny pieces and assembled later — the actors often film the ending months before the beginning.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      First Aid Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Cook, grow & help

      First aid club is the helping club: what to do in the small emergencies — a scrape, a bruise, a scared sibling — and how to call for the big ones. The card prints the club’s two skills — Help & Care — knowing the steps and staying kind while doing them. This card’s job: make the child the calmest helper in the room.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “First aid club! Helpers know three things: check, call, care — check what happened, call a grown-up, keep the hurt person company. Help & Care: brave helpers practice BEFORE the emergency.”

      Try this

      Role-play the drill: a stuffed animal has a scrape. Clean the pretend wound, apply the pretend bandage, say the calming words. Then rehearse the real phone number out loud, twice.

      Quick parent note

      Emergency numbers differ by country — 911 in the US, 999 in the UK, 112 across Europe — knowing YOURS is the first-aid club’s graduation exam.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Gymnastics Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Move & play

      Gymnastics club is the body-control club: rolls, balances, bridges and the quiet strength under every wobbly hold. The card prints the club’s two skills — Strength & Flexibility — power and stretch, trained as a pair. This card’s job: put the first safe roll and the first proud balance on the living-room floor.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Gymnastics club! Strong AND stretchy — that is the whole sport. Strength & Flexibility: tuck the chin for a roll, hold the arms for a balance. Show me your strongest still statue.”

      Try this

      The animal warm-up before any rolling: bear walk, crab walk, frog jump, flamingo stand. Two minutes of animals and the body is ready for real skills on a soft surface.

      Quick parent note

      Gymnasts train falls on purpose — learning to fall safely is a real skill with a name, and it makes the landing braver than the takeoff.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Horse Riding Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Move & play

      Horse riding club is the half-ton-friend club: helmets on, hooves brushing, and the slow trust between rider and horse. The card prints the club’s two skills — Courage & Care — being brave around something big and gentle with it. This card’s job: make the stable feel like the most exciting classroom there is.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Horse riding club! Horses are big and kind — we move slowly, speak softly, and a grown-up or instructor is always there. Courage & Care: riders are brave AND gentle. Can you hello the horse with a flat hand?”

      Try this

      Pre-riding practice: groom a friend’s dog with a soft brush the way riders groom horses — slow strokes, kind voice. Then practice mounting posture on a chair, back tall, eyes up.

      Quick parent note

      Horses read feelings through body language — a nervous rider makes a nervous horse, which is why riding teachers care so much about calm.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Journaling Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Read & write

      Journaling club is the notebook club: one page a day for whatever matters — the best bite of lunch, the unfair moment, the dream that woke you. The card prints the club’s two skills — Reflect & Express — thinking back and writing it down. This card’s job: give the child a private place where the day can land.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Journaling club! This notebook is yours — spelling does not matter, truth does. Reflect & Express: writers write what the day was really like. What was today’s headline?”

      Try this

      Three-lines-a-day rule: today I saw / today I felt / tomorrow I hope. Three lines takes two minutes, and two minutes keeps the habit alive for months.

      Quick parent note

      Captain’s logs, flight logs, diaries kept by explorers — most of history’s best stories survived because somebody wrote small, honest notes daily.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Lego Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Make & build

      Lego club is the brick club: a pile of colors, a plan (or none), and the click that means the idea is growing. The card prints the club’s two skills — Build & Create — following instructions and inventing past them. This card’s job: make the first build the beginning, not the end.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Lego club! Bricks first, then a bridge, then a whole city. Build & Create: builders sort, stack, test — and rebuild when the tower leans. What are we building today?”

      Try this

      The rebuild challenge: follow a small set’s instructions once, then take it apart and build something completely new from the same pieces. The second build is where creativity lives.

      Quick parent note

      The name LEGO comes from the Danish phrase leg godt — play well — which the company discovered later also means I put together in Latin.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Martial Arts Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Move & play

      Martial arts club is the respect-first club: bow in, listen hard, practice the kick a hundred calm times. The card prints the club’s two skills — Discipline & Strength — self-control and the body it builds. This card’s job: bring the dojo’s first lesson home — the quiet before the movement.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Martial arts club! Every class starts with a bow — respect for the teacher, the space and ourselves. Discipline & Strength: martial artists are strong AND calm. Can you stand in ready stance for five breaths?”

      Try this

      Home kata practice: three slow moves — block, punch, block — in front of a mirror, five times slow, five times quick. Slow builds the shape; fast builds the power.

      Quick parent note

      The colored belt system started in judo in Japan with just white, brown and black — everything else was added later to give students milestones.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Nature Crafts Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Make & build

      Nature crafts club is the walk-first club: gather leaves, sticks, stones and petals on the way, then let the making begin. The card prints the club’s two skills — Collect & Create — foraging with care and building with what the path gave. This card’s job: turn the backyard into a craft store with no price tags.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Nature crafts club! We take only what has already fallen — leaves, twigs, seed pods. Collect & Create: nature gives the materials, we give the idea. What is that leaf becoming?”

      Try this

      Leaf-and-stick animal gallery: flat leaf = owl body, twig legs, stone head, glue on card. Three animals make a gallery; a gallery needs an opening night with juice.

      Quick parent note

      The fancy word is ephemeral art — art made from things that fade — and galleries around the world hang photographs of leaf art exactly like yours.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Photography Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Think & solve

      Photography club is the frame club: look, choose, click — the art of deciding what belongs in the rectangle. The card prints the club’s two skills — Observe & Create — seeing carefully and keeping what you saw. This card’s job: make the child the family’s official eye.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Photography club! A photographer asks: what is the most interesting thing right here? Observe & Create: steady hands, one subject, click. What will your first photo be of?”

      Try this

      The five-photo scavenger hunt: something red, something tiny, something that makes you laugh, something from below, something that shows today. Five pictures, one story.

      Quick parent note

      The first photograph ever taken needed eight hours of exposure — the sun moved so much during the shot that both sides of the street got sunlight.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Poetry Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Read & write

      Poetry club is the short-words club: few lines, big feelings, and the freedom to compare the moon to a pancake. The card prints the club’s two skills — Words & Feelings — choosing exact words and saying what the heart is doing. This card’s job: get the first poem written and read out loud, proudly.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Poetry club! Poems are small — five lines can hold a whole feeling. Words & Feelings: poets pick words the way painters pick colors. What does rain sound like to you?”

      Try this

      List poem recipe: I like / I wonder / I remember / I dream / I wish — one line each, and the last line is read with the biggest voice in the house.

      Quick parent note

      Haiku poems are only seventeen sounds long in Japanese — three short lines — and yet whole seasons fit inside them.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Pottery Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Make & build

      Pottery club is the mud-that-becomes-things club: wet clay, patient hands, a bowl or a cup that came out of nothing but a lump. The card prints the club’s two skills — Shape & Imagine — forming the material and picturing it finished. This card’s job: let the first pinch pot earn a place at dinner.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Pottery club! Clay listens to hands — press slow, turn the lump, press again. Shape & Imagine: potters see the bowl inside the mud. What are we making for the kitchen?”

      Try this

      Pinch-pot start: push a thumb into a ball of clay and pinch the walls thin by turning and squeezing — the oldest pottery trick on Earth, still the first thing students learn.

      Quick parent note

      Pottery survives when empires do not — archaeologists date ancient cities by the styles of their broken pots, shard by shard.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Puppetry Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Perform & sing

      Puppetry club is the backstage club: build a character from a sock or a paper bag, give it a voice, and let it take the stage while you hide. The card prints the club’s two skills — Create & Perform — making the character and bringing it alive. This card’s job: get the first show booked for the hallway wall.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Puppetry club! The puppet is shy until it has a voice — high, low, growly? Create & Perform: puppeteers build the character, then act. What is your puppet’s name?”

      Try this

      Doorway stage: a sheet hung in a doorway, knees behind it, one puppet at a time peeking over. A two-scene show — hello, joke, goodbye — is a complete first production.

      Quick parent note

      Puppetry is thousands of years old and appears on every continent — some historians think puppets were telling stories before writing existed.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Robotics Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Make & build

      Robotics club is the build-a-helper club: motors, sensors, wheels and a machine that does what you designed it to do. The card prints the club’s two skills — Build & Invent — constructing the machine and dreaming up what it should do next. This card’s job: reframe the household machines as robots that started as ideas.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Robotics club! A robot is a machine that follows a plan — vacuum robots, factory arms, the Mars rover. Build & Invent: engineers build, test, improve. What job should YOUR robot do?”

      Try this

      Human robot course: one player is the robot (eyes closed or blindfolded), the other gives exact commands — two steps forward, quarter turn left. Reach the teddy bear: mission accomplished.

      Quick parent note

      Robot comes from the Czech word robota, meaning forced work — named in a 1920 play about machines that did the labor.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Science Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Think & solve

      Science club is the question club: guess, test, observe, and the honest moment when the answer surprises everyone. The card prints the club’s two skills — Explore & Experiment — curiosity in the field and careful tests in the kitchen lab. This card’s job: run the first experiment the house cannot stop talking about.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Science club! Scientists write their guess down BEFORE the test — that is what makes it fair. Explore & Experiment: we ask, we try, we look closely. What is our first question?”

      Try this

      Sink-or-float census: fill the sink, gather ten small objects, have everyone vote sink or float before each one lands. Wrong predictions are the best part — they mean a discovery is happening.

      Quick parent note

      Real scientists keep experiment notebooks with the date on every page — because a result nobody wrote down is a result nobody can check.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Skateboarding Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Move & play

      Skateboarding club is the rolling club: board, helmet, pads, and the specific courage of pushing off for the very first glide. The card prints the club’s two skills — Balance & Confidence — staying over the board and trying again after every tumble. This card’s job: make the first safe ride on flat ground the milestone.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Skateboarding club! Helmet, pads, flat ground — then one gentle push. Balance & Confidence: skaters fall, get up, and fall better. Can you stand on the board while it stands still?”

      Try this

      Carpet first: put the board on a rug and practice stance and weight shifts where it cannot roll. Then grass, then smooth pavement — each surface one notch braver.

      Quick parent note

      Skateboarding was born from surfing — surfers in California wanted something to ride when the waves were flat, so they put wheels under a plank.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Table Tennis Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Move & play

      Table tennis club is the small-table, fast-ball club: paddles, a net, rallies that get quicker and gigglier every point. The card prints the club’s two skills — React & Play — fast eyes and the love of the rally. This card’s job: hold the first rally longer than anyone thought possible.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Table tennis club! Little swings — the ball is light, the table is close. React & Play: watch the ball all the way to your paddle. Ready — one bounce on each side, how many can we keep going?”

      Try this

      Cooperative rallies, not competition: count consecutive hits together and try to beat the family record. The record chase makes every player better without a single lost point.

      Quick parent note

      Table tennis balls once measured 38 millimeters, now 40 — the bigger ball flies a little slower so audiences could follow the world’s fastest rallies on TV.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Tennis Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Move & play

      Tennis club is the court club: racket, yellow ball, a net, and the fun of a game where every point starts with a friendly serve. The card prints the club’s two skills — Move & Compete — covering the court and playing to win with grace. This card’s job: land the first balls over the net and keep the feet moving.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Tennis club! Side-on stance, smooth swing — the ball loves a calm racket. Move & Compete: tennis players run AND score with a handshake after. Can you bounce the ball ten times on the racket?”

      Try this

      Racket-control ladder before any serving: ten bounces flat, ten bounces on the racket edge, walk while bouncing, then a partner toss-and-hit over a bench net. The ladder makes the court feel smaller.

      Quick parent note

      Tennis scores go 15, 30, 40 — probably from clock faces long ago, where each point moved the hand a quarter turn and 45 got shortened along the way.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · EXTRA-CURRICULAR ACTIVITIES · AGES 3–12 YEARS

      Volunteering Flashcard for Kids

      Ages 6+Cook, grow & help

      Volunteering club is the helping-others club: food drives, park cleanups, helping neighbors — the clubs that give instead of take. The card prints the club’s two skills — Share & Support — giving time and lifting someone else’s week. This card’s job: make the first act of service feel like belonging.

      Teaching tips

      Say it together

      “Volunteering club! Helpers do not need money — they need time and kind eyes. Share & Support: volunteers see a problem and offer a hand. What can we do for someone this week?”

      Try this

      The two-basket donation: with the child, fill one basket of toys to give away and one box of pantry food for a local drive. The child carries the delivery — carrying it is the moment.

      Quick parent note

      Volunteers are the world’s biggest workforce without a salary — hundreds of millions of people help every year just because someone should.

      Teach it, step by step
